accepted_claim: For the recorded CrewAI 1.15.21 same-process synchronous ToolUsage._use retry boundary, an unguarded tool whose external effect commits and then raises before returning can be re-entered by the built-in retry and produce a second external effect for one logical action.
admission_interpretation: The source record is admitted as bounded external evidence because its published bytes are pinned, the downloaded artifact hashes match its manifest, and the raw 90-trial receipts independently recompute to the claimed case distributions and event ordering. Admission verifies the evidence record and its internal claim boundary; it is not an independent rerun of CrewAI.
non_claims: No independent rerun of the 90 trials was performed by ContractGraph-QA.
The publication CI job explicitly did not execute the original experiment.
The record does not establish the original execution time or a clean original checkout.
No process crash, worker replacement, fresh-process recovery, checkpoint restore, or external retrigger is measured.
No real LLM or provider is measured.
No idempotency guard or deduplication boundary is measured.
Host power-loss durability of the external ledger is not measured.
This does not establish exactly-once execution for CrewAI generally or for untested versions and paths.

next_test.question: Can an observer outside the runtime bind the same stable logical action identity to a durable pre-execution claim and an external effect receipt, then prevent or classify redispatch without treating persisted state as fresh execution authority?
next_test.boundary: stable action identity -> fresh authorization -> one-use permit -> dispatch -> external receipt/read-back
